facts.text: I asked whether the lyrics “Some faces I know… London to Tokyo… LA to Monaco” could be referring to his fans at his concerts.
I asked whether the lyrics “Some faces I know… Doesn’t matter where I go… I see you” might refer to seeing one particular person standing out.
I said “Near-Life Experience” makes me feel nostalgic and also a bit sour.
I said I like the idea of a “near-life experience.”
I said I think a “near-life experience” makes me think of being depressed or in a very low mood.
I said I think a “near-life experience” involves doing something that brings closer to almost feeling alive.
I said I interpret the lyrics as someone saying “you’re almost there, you’re almost living up to the full potential life can offer.”
I said the “near-life experience” is a nice subversion of the casual “near-death experience.”
I said I like the idea conveyed by the verses “I didn’t do this for you… I did this for me.”
I said the idea in “I didn’t do this for you… I did this for me” reinforces personal freedom, independency, and sincere personal expression.
I said I like the idea of “And now you’ll see what I’ve achieved… from the depths of my despair.”
I said it feels real to me that harder or more depressing moments in life can help people grow and become more resilient to future obstacles.
I said “Altar in the sun” wasn’t existential and is rather hedonistic.

keyphrases: I didn’t do this for you
